title: Transparency, accountability, and fairness baseline
text: Use a risk-based approach to ensure automated decisions are transparent, accountable, lawful, and fair. Translate impact level into concrete controls (testing, oversight, disclosure, recourse). Maintain artifacts that explain what was assessed and what actions were taken.

title: Algorithmic Impact Assessment as a deployment gate
text: Assess impact of automated decision systems before deployment and tailor controls to impact level. Use the assessment to decide required transparency, human involvement, and monitoring. Keep the assessment as an executive-ready decision trace.

title: Transparency and public reporting expectations
text: Provide transparency about automated decision systems and publish information to support accountability. Define what information is disclosed and how it is kept current. Public reporting becomes an externalized explainability mechanism.

title: Quality assurance through testing and monitoring
text: Ensure quality and effectiveness through testing, monitoring, and governance controls. Define acceptance thresholds and post-deployment drift monitoring. Maintain evidence that issues are detected and acted on consistently.

title: Recourse mechanisms for affected individuals
text: Provide individuals with information about recourse options and how to challenge outcomes. Operationalize this with clear contact paths and response SLAs. Recourse is a key part of explainability: it makes decisions contestable and correctable.

title: Human involvement proportional to impact
text: Ensure human involvement and oversight proportional to impact, including escalation and review for high-impact cases. Define override authority and logging. Human involvement should be designed as an operational capability, not a symbolic control.
